parameters.name: Total sleep time
parameters.whatToTrack: Total sleep time per 24 hours from wrist actigraphy
parameters.targetText: 8.5-hour sleep opportunity recommended; NASA does not set a minimum total sleep time
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
parameters.countermeasures: Circadian LED lighting; Designated relaxation and self-care time
parameters.consequence: Cumulative sleep debt, daytime sleepiness, slower reaction time, poorer decision-making and mood, reduced recovery.
parameters.operationalImpact: Higher error rates on critical tasks; degraded EVA, docking and flight performance.
parameters.notes: The 8.5 h figure is the scheduled opportunity, not a measured sleep floor.
parameters.bandLabel: App operational band. NASA-STD-3001 recommends an 8.5-hour sleep opportunity and sets no minimum total sleep time.

parameters.name: Sleep-wake timing
parameters.whatToTrack: Bedtime, wake time and night-to-night variability
parameters.targetText: Keep timing consistent; avoid critical tasks during the 1-7 AM circadian nadir
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
parameters.consequence: Circadian desynchronization, poor sleep quality, insomnia, daytime fatigue and mood disturbance.
parameters.operationalImpact: Alertness misaligned with critical task times; impaired judgment and teamwork.
parameters.notes: Circadian entrainment requires consistent sleep timing day to day.

parameters.name: Sleep efficiency
parameters.whatToTrack: Sleep efficiency = total sleep time / time in bed
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
parameters.consequence: Fragmented, non-restorative sleep and reduced recovery.
parameters.operationalImpact: Lower vigilance and cognitive performance; fatigue accumulation.

parameters.name: Sleep onset latency
parameters.whatToTrack: Time from lights-out to sleep onset
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
parameters.consequence: Difficulty falling asleep and shortened sleep.
parameters.operationalImpact: Reduced total sleep and next-day performance decline.

parameters.name: Sleep fragmentation
parameters.whatToTrack: Wake after sleep onset and number of awakenings
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
parameters.consequence: Frequent awakenings and poor sleep continuity.
parameters.operationalImpact: Daytime fatigue and attention lapses.

parameters.name: Light exposure at the eye
parameters.whatToTrack: Illuminance and RGB light from wrist sensors; melanopic EDI estimate
parameters.targetText: Daytime at least 250 melanopic EDI lux; pre-sleep 8 +/- 2; sleep period at most 0.02 lux
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules; Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
parameters.consequence: Circadian misalignment, melatonin suppression, delayed sleep onset and poor sleep quality; low daytime light reduces alertness.
parameters.operationalImpact: Shifted sleep-wake cycle, fatigue, mood and performance effects.
parameters.notes: Melanopic values are estimated from photopic and RGB channels.

parameters.name: Core body temperature
parameters.whatToTrack: Core temperature time series and circadian phase
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track circadian trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
parameters.consequence: Thermoregulatory strain and disrupted circadian rhythm and sleep timing.
parameters.operationalImpact: Heat stress during exercise or EVA; poor sleep.
parameters.notes: Measured with a forehead heat-flux sensor.

parameters.name: Work/rest schedule
parameters.whatToTrack: Scheduled sleep opportunity, duty hours, exercise and task timing
parameters.targetText: 8.5 h sleep period plus 2 h pre-sleep and 1.5 h post-sleep; limits on duty and workload
parameters.monitoringSource: Sleep logs and questionnaires; crew schedule
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules; Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
parameters.consequence: Fatigue, burnout, circadian disruption and sleep loss.
parameters.operationalImpact: Critical-task errors; degraded crew performance and safety.
parameters.notes: NASA requires that schedule limits be established.

parameters.name: Exercise dose
parameters.whatToTrack: Session completion, duration, type and weekly consistency
parameters.targetText: 1.5 hours per day, 6-7 days per week (ISS practice)
parameters.thresholdBasis: ISS operational practice (NASA Human Research Program)
parameters.monitoringSource: ARED; CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness; Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
parameters.countermeasures: Resistance training 1.5 hours per day; Aerobic exercise 1.5 hours per day
parameters.consequence: Muscle atrophy, bone loss, aerobic deconditioning and reduced cardiovascular capacity.
parameters.operationalImpact: Difficulty with EVA tasks, emergency egress and post-flight recovery; higher injury risk.
parameters.notes: NASA-STD-3001 sets outcome thresholds, not a daily duration.
parameters.bandLabel: ISS practice is about 1.5 hours per day, 6-7 days per week. Band applied to the 7-day average of watch active minutes.

parameters.name: Exercise type split
parameters.whatToTrack: Resistive versus aerobic minutes and sessions
parameters.targetText: Include both resistance and aerobic exercise each week
parameters.monitoringSource: ARED; CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
parameters.countermeasures: Resistance training 1.5 hours per day; Aerobic exercise 1.5 hours per day
parameters.consequence: Imbalance between strength and aerobic fitness; incomplete protection of bone and muscle.
parameters.operationalImpact: Reduced EVA capability and injury resilience.

parameters.name: External load and repetitions
parameters.whatToTrack: Applied load and repetitions on the resistive device
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric target; track training volume and progression
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness; Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
parameters.consequence: Insufficient mechanical loading, leading to muscle and bone loss.
parameters.operationalImpact: Strength falling below the 80% threshold and reduced task performance.

parameters.name: Power output and heart rate
parameters.whatToTrack: Power, speed, duration and heart-rate response during aerobic exercise
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric target; track training intensity
parameters.monitoringSource: CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
parameters.consequence: Inadequate aerobic stimulus and VO2max decline.
parameters.operationalImpact: Fatigue during EVA and reduced endurance.

parameters.name: Aerobic capacity (VO2max)
parameters.whatToTrack: VO2max from periodic fitness tests or estimates
parameters.targetText: At least 32.9 ml/min/kg for microgravity EVA; 36.5 for surface EVA; at least 80% of pre-mission
parameters.monitoringSource: CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
parameters.consequence: Aerobic deconditioning and inability to sustain EVA workloads.
parameters.operationalImpact: Compromised EVA performance, fatigue and higher injury risk.

parameters.name: Muscle strength
parameters.whatToTrack: Deadlift and bench press relative to body weight; in-mission strength retention
parameters.targetText: At least 80% of baseline in flight; pre-mission deadlift 1.3-1.6x body weight and bench press 0.8-1.0x
parameters.cadence: Pre-mission; periodic in flight; 5-7 days after landing
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness; Risk of Injury and Compromised Performance from Spacewalks
parameters.consequence: Loss of muscle strength and power, joint instability and fall risk.
parameters.operationalImpact: Difficulty handling suits and tools, performing EVA and egressing in an emergency.

parameters.name: Bone mineral density
parameters.whatToTrack: BMD of total hip, lumbar spine and femoral neck by DXA
parameters.targetText: Hip and spine at least 95% of pre-mission; femoral neck at least 90%
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
parameters.countermeasures: Resistive exercise for bone; Bisphosphonate medication
parameters.consequence: Bone loss, fractures and premature osteoporosis; hypercalciuria and kidney stones.
parameters.operationalImpact: Fracture risk during landing or surface operations; renal stone event.

parameters.name: Energy intake
parameters.whatToTrack: Calories consumed versus estimated expenditure
parameters.targetText: Match intake to expenditure; no numeric NASA intake standard in reviewed sources
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
parameters.countermeasures: Crew menu tasting and selection; Nutritionally enhanced diets
parameters.consequence: Weight loss, muscle wasting, fatigue, immune suppression and poor recovery.
parameters.operationalImpact: Performance decrement, illness and reduced countermeasure effectiveness.

parameters.name: Macronutrients
parameters.whatToTrack: Carbohydrate, protein and fat intake
parameters.targetText: Monitor intake; no numeric NASA targets in reviewed sources
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
parameters.consequence: Insufficient protein for muscle maintenance and poor energy availability.
parameters.operationalImpact: Muscle loss and fatigue.

parameters.name: Micronutrients
parameters.whatToTrack: Vitamin D, omega-3 fatty acids, lutein and other micronutrients
parameters.targetText: Vitamin D supplementation required; dose is program-defined; monitor other micronutrients periodically
parameters.monitoringSource: Food and diet logs; periodic laboratory samples
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition; Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
parameters.consequence: Bone loss from low vitamin D, immune dysfunction, and vision and cardiovascular effects.
parameters.operationalImpact: Higher risk of fracture, infection and ocular changes.

parameters.name: Sodium intake
parameters.whatToTrack: Sodium content of the diet
parameters.targetText: Reduced-sodium space food; no numeric target in reviewed sources
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition; Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
parameters.consequence: Excess sodium may contribute to cardiovascular and fluid-balance problems.
parameters.operationalImpact: Cardiovascular risk and blood-pressure changes.

parameters.name: Food variety and acceptability
parameters.whatToTrack: Meal acceptability ratings and menu variety
parameters.targetText: More than 200 foods and beverages available aboard the ISS; rate meals to prevent menu fatigue
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
parameters.countermeasures: Crew menu tasting and selection; Lower-sodium, varied space food
parameters.consequence: Menu fatigue, reduced intake and weight loss.
parameters.operationalImpact: Inadequate nutrition and performance decline.

parameters.name: Menu fatigue
parameters.whatToTrack: Self-reported boredom with the menu and food intake decline
parameters.targetText: No numeric NASA limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
parameters.consequence: Declining food intake and morale.
parameters.operationalImpact: Nutritional deficits and lower crew morale.

parameters.name: Fluid intake
parameters.whatToTrack: Fluid consumed per day (water, beverages, foods)
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric intake standard in reviewed sources; app default 2-3 L/day to be set with the flight surgeon
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes (renal stone risk); Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
parameters.consequence: Dehydration, orthostatic intolerance, fainting at landing, kidney-stone risk, fatigue and cognitive decline.
parameters.operationalImpact: Syncope during landing or egress; renal stone event; reduced performance.
parameters.notes: Dehydration can worsen orthostatic intolerance and renal stone risk.

parameters.name: Urine color and specific gravity
parameters.whatToTrack: Self-reported urine color or point-of-care specific gravity
parameters.targetText: No NASA threshold; trend with the clinical team
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
parameters.consequence: Under-hydration or over-hydration.
parameters.operationalImpact: Impaired thermoregulation and cardiovascular stability.

parameters.name: Water availability and quality
parameters.whatToTrack: Potable water supply and quality monitoring
parameters.targetText: Potable water must meet spacecraft water exposure guidelines
parameters.consequence: Gastrointestinal infection or chemical exposure.
parameters.operationalImpact: Crew illness and mission impact.
parameters.notes: Quality monitoring covers chemical and microbiological safety.

parameters.name: Renal stone risk markers
parameters.whatToTrack: Hypercalciuria and other urine markers
parameters.targetText: No numeric NASA threshold; monitor alongside bone health
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
parameters.consequence: Kidney stone formation.
parameters.operationalImpact: Severe pain and a medical event that may affect the mission.
parameters.notes: Bone loss raises calcium excretion and kidney-stone risk.

parameters.name: Mood
parameters.whatToTrack: Daily mood rating
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend against personal baseline
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
parameters.countermeasures: Self-care including journaling; Virtual contact with family and medical staff
parameters.consequence: Depression, anxiety, low morale, and sleep and appetite changes.
parameters.operationalImpact: Impaired decision-making, teamwork and mission performance.
parameters.bandLabel: App screening band for sustained low mood over the last 7 days on the 1-5 check-in scale. NASA sets no numeric limit; compare with the personal baseline.

parameters.name: Stress
parameters.whatToTrack: Perceived stress rating
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
parameters.consequence: Cognitive impairment, sleep disruption, and cardiovascular and immune effects.
parameters.operationalImpact: Errors, fatigue and conflict.
parameters.bandLabel: App screening band. NASA tracks stress as a trend with no numeric limit; this band is an app default for early warning.

parameters.name: Workload
parameters.whatToTrack: Perceived workload and task pressure
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders; Risk of Inadequate Systems Operations Support
parameters.consequence: Fatigue, burnout and stress.
parameters.operationalImpact: Performance decrement and safety risk.

parameters.name: Sleepiness and fatigue
parameters.whatToTrack: Subjective sleepiness and fatigue rating
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend and task timing
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
parameters.consequence: Attention lapses and slowed reaction time.
parameters.operationalImpact: Critical-task errors, especially during EVA and docking.

parameters.name: Team climate and cohesion
parameters.whatToTrack: Team check-in and conflict indicators
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Inadequate Teamwork
parameters.consequence: Conflict, miscommunication and reduced cohesion.
parameters.operationalImpact: Mission performance and safety decrement.

parameters.name: Privacy and social support
parameters.whatToTrack: Perceived privacy, isolation and contact with family
parameters.targetText: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders; Risk of Inadequate Teamwork
parameters.countermeasures: Virtual contact with family and medical staff; Privacy-maximizing habitat design
parameters.consequence: Isolation distress, homesickness, and sleep and mood problems.
parameters.operationalImpact: Morale and performance decline.

parameters.name: Cognitive performance
parameters.whatToTrack: Reaction time, memory, attention and executive function
parameters.targetText: Compare with personal pre-mission baseline
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders; Risk of Inadequate Systems Operations Support
parameters.consequence: Decline in attention, memory and reaction time.
parameters.operationalImpact: Decision-making errors and safety risk.

parameters.name: Self-care adherence
parameters.whatToTrack: Journaling, relaxation and recreation practice
parameters.targetText: No numeric target; encourage daily practice
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
parameters.countermeasures: Self-care including journaling; Designated relaxation and self-care time
parameters.consequence: Burnout, poor coping and psychological decline.
parameters.operationalImpact: Reduced resilience and performance.

parameters.name: General symptom diary
parameters.whatToTrack: Structured body-system symptom report with severity and duration
parameters.targetText: No numeric threshold; structured reporting and escalation
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses; Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions; Risk of Hypoxia
parameters.countermeasures: Biological sample monitoring for latent viruses
parameters.consequence: Undetected infection, immune alteration or other medical condition.
parameters.operationalImpact: Progression to serious illness and mission impact.

parameters.name: Vision changes
parameters.whatToTrack: Blurring, visual field changes, flashes or distortion
parameters.targetText: Any new visual change triggers a same-day ocular check (app default)
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
parameters.countermeasures: Eye-protective nutritional supplements; Mechanical interventions for headward fluid shift
parameters.consequence: SANS with optic nerve swelling, retinal folds and brain swelling; possible long-term vision loss.
parameters.operationalImpact: Visual performance decrement and long-term health risk.

parameters.name: Headache, confusion or dizziness
parameters.whatToTrack: Neurological symptoms and timing
parameters.targetText: Red flag for hypoxia or CO2 exposure; check cabin oxygen and CO2 (app default)
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Hypoxia
parameters.consequence: Hypoxia or CO2 toxicity with cognitive impairment.
parameters.operationalImpact: Incapacitation risk and task errors.

parameters.name: Joint pain after EVA
parameters.whatToTrack: Joint pain, skin mottling or other pressure-related symptoms after a spacewalk
parameters.targetText: Red flag for decompression sickness; follow the spacewalk abort protocol (app default)
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Decompression Sickness
parameters.countermeasures: Prebreathe oxygen protocols; Spacewalk abort and repressurization protocol
parameters.consequence: Decompression sickness, tissue damage and, in severe cases, stroke-like symptoms.
parameters.operationalImpact: Medical emergency during or after a spacewalk.

parameters.name: Skin rash or cold sore
parameters.whatToTrack: Rashes, cold sores and other skin or viral signs
parameters.targetText: Report for review; may indicate immune alteration or latent virus reactivation
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses; Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions
parameters.countermeasures: Biological sample monitoring for latent viruses; Pre-launch exposure restriction
parameters.consequence: Immune alteration, latent virus reactivation and infection.
parameters.operationalImpact: Crew illness and reduced performance.

parameters.name: Gastrointestinal symptoms
parameters.whatToTrack: Nausea, diarrhea, constipation and appetite change
parameters.targetText: Report for review; may relate to nutrition or microbiome changes
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions; Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
parameters.consequence: Infection, microbiome disturbance or malabsorption.
parameters.operationalImpact: Illness and nutrition deficit.

parameters.name: Injury and pain
parameters.whatToTrack: Musculoskeletal pain, sprains or injuries
parameters.targetText: Report for review; track cause and recovery
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of Injury and Compromised Performance from Spacewalks; Risk of Injury from Dynamic Loads
parameters.countermeasures: Improved spacesuit design; Seat and restraint design standards
parameters.consequence: Musculoskeletal injury, pain and impaired mobility.
parameters.operationalImpact: Reduced task performance; EVA and landing risk.

parameters.name: Medication and supplement use
parameters.whatToTrack: Dose, indication, adherence and side effects
parameters.targetText: Log every use; review side effects with the flight surgeon
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules; Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
parameters.consequence: Side effects, drug interactions, impaired sleep or cognition, and dependence.
parameters.operationalImpact: Performance and safety risk.
parameters.notes: Includes sleep aids, caffeine, painkillers and vitamin D.

parameters.name: Resting heart rate
parameters.whatToTrack: Resting heart rate from the wearable
parameters.targetText: 50–100 bpm at rest (app screening range)
parameters.thresholdBasis: App screening default; the NASA guideline file sets no numeric heart-rate limit.
parameters.relatedRisks: Risk of cardiovascular deconditioning and orthostatic intolerance
parameters.countermeasures: Sit down and stop activity. Breathe slowly for 2–3 minutes, drink water, and recheck your heart rate. If it stays above 120 bpm, or you feel chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath, contact the flight surgeon now.
parameters.consequence: A high resting heart rate can reflect strain, dehydration, fever, stress or a heart rhythm problem.
parameters.operationalImpact: Reduced exercise tolerance and higher risk during EVA or emergency egress.
parameters.bandLabel: App screening range for resting heart rate. NASA sets no numeric heart-rate limit; 50–100 bpm is the healthy band, 40–50 and 100–120 are caution zones, and outside 40–120 is urgent.
